title: The Seeds of Laziness
text: “Peep!”
Since my Father had returned, we went back to the carriage as planned.
“A name for the new baby, huh…”
“One possibility is ‘Navy-chan,’ I suppose.”
“That’s pretty straightforward. In the future, were there any names like ‘Ai’ derived from indigo—a color similar to ‘Kon’?”
“That’s right. That’s why I thought I’d ask my Father if a different name might be better.”
“Still, though…”

Looking at the new Filolial-sama, who was already beginning to take on her second form—resembling a manju bun—my Father fell deep in thought. Then he reached out and gently stroked the area around her throat. The new Filolial-sama narrowed her eyes in apparent pleasure.
“According to Motoyasu-kun’s memories, this isn’t the same child with the same name, is it?”
“That’s right.”
“Well then, it might be difficult to give her the same name… Hmm…”
It’s navy blue, after all. It’s hard to call it black—it’s more of a deep blue hue.
“Well then, how about ‘Hanada,’ taken from ‘Kokihanada,’ an old term for navy blue?”
“Father, you really know your names, don’t you?”
I, Motoyasu, am truly impressed by the depth of my father’s knowledge. He has a way of thinking I simply don’t possess.
“I learned it a long time ago as the name of a hidden dungeon in a video game. I just happened to remember it.”
“Is that so? Then would that name be all right?”
“I just said it out loud, but I get the feeling it’s not really a name you’d give a girl.”
“Boo……”
“Huh? You mean, since she hatched around the time we defeated the Bio Plant, why not name her after that? You think? That’s not a bad idea either.”
“Boo”
“Another place name where it hatched, huh? Yeah, that’s a reasonable choice.”
Father is taking the Lazy Pig’s advice to heart and checking the map several times.
“Big bro, big bro! This little one has such a beautiful, night-like color—how about ‘Yozora-chan’? Or maybe ‘Hoshi-chan’?”
“It’s not bad, but… hmm.”
“Piyo?”
Father seems to be struggling to come up with a name for the new Filolial-sama. I sometimes struggle with choosing names, too.
“Oink…”

“Huh? Since this is a hassle, I’ll just take it from the phrase ‘surpassing the master,’ left behind by a past hero… No way! That’s out of the question! Sure, Filolial looks like a horse, but ‘Ranhomare’ is just cruel!”

Oh? That’s not a bad name for something the Lazy Pig came up with. It seems that many of Filolial-sama’s common names do sound like those of racehorses. So there’s no need to dismiss them outright. In fact, Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan don’t seem to have any issues with the names at all; they’re just tilting their heads in confusion at my Father’s objections.
“What should I do…? Hmm? Following Keel-kun’s example of naming after celestial bodies, how about ‘Luna’—from the moon?”
“Ooh! That’s a very girly name.”
“It rolls off the tongue nicely—I think it’s a good choice, bro.”
“Boo!”

It’s not a bad idea. I usually decide on names without thinking too deeply about it. If it were up to me, I’d definitely go with Navy-chan. But I do think Luna-chan, as Father suggested, isn’t a bad choice either.
“Then this little one’s name will be Luna!”
“Piyo!”
Luna-chan chirped cheerfully.
“Well… for now, you gluttonous lot, I guess I’ll cook up some chimera meat for dinner tonight.”
“Yay!”

And so, we all gathered around the table, happily enjoying the meal Father had prepared, and the day came to an end. Then, as night fell, Father and I took a break from our Magic studies to work on our bio-plant research. That said, Father handled the fine-tuning.
“Well, we’ve ensured safety for now, so we need a place to conduct experiments.”
“Oink…”
“Huh? Should we use the estate managed by Elena’s parents this time? Well… I suppose so.”
“Oink.”

That Lazy Pig is designating his own estate as the site to plant the bio-plant seeds. I know all about it. Pigs have a keen sense of smell, after all. I’m sure he’s picking up the scent of money. Even in my original world, finding truffles is a pig’s job. I suppose that’s just his specialty.
“Yeah, we can make all sorts of fine adjustments. So what?”
“Oink.”
The Lazy Pig is oinking at my Father over and over while swaying in his hammock. Each time, my Father just nodded in agreement. It seems they’re discussing the bio-plants.
“I see. That might actually be a good idea. Though the final adjustments will have to be made on Elena’s estate.”
“What did you decide?”
“Well, we’re talking about changing the design of the bio-plants for sale, and the ones we’ll use exclusively for trading and harvesting.”

My father told me about the plan he’d discussed with the Lazy Pig. Specifically, when modifying the bio-plants, we’ll minimize the risk of mutation as much as possible and improve them for maximum productivity. However, if people can just harvest them without doing anything, it’s obvious that those who receive them will become lazy.

After all, even though there’s a famine, these are miraculous plants that solve the food problem simply by being harvested. When people can live without going hungry, they’ll get lazy. Or perhaps it would be the start of foolish conflicts.
Happiness earned through one’s own efforts is many times more wonderful than happiness simply given. As expected of Father.

“At first, we’ll go around as peddlers, selling the fruits we harvest in various places. Then, once the food situation has stabilized to a certain extent, we’ll provide seeds for the bio-plant—which will wither away in the blink of an eye if not properly managed—and solve the people’s fundamental problem.”
“Aren’t you going to sell them at a high price right from the start?”

“I thought about that too, but when it comes to raising funds, you gain trust by doling it out little by little. No matter how much word of mouth calls me a saint, it hasn’t spread far enough yet… Of course, I’ll plant the seeds immediately in areas with the highest urgency.”
“Booh…”
“Apparently, according to what Elena said, the waves are causing crop failures. I hear a food crisis is emerging.”

So, we’ll build trust by distributing food while peddling goods using Father’s horse-drawn carriage. The food crisis is certainly a critical issue. After all, there were plenty of people suffering from hunger in the original world and in previous loops as well.

“But there’s a limit to just selling food door-to-door, so we’ll eventually start selling the seeds themselves. By then, they’ll trust us, so I think they’ll manage them properly. But you never know what people will do, and we can’t trust anyone who’d let the seeds we give them wither away.”

Come to think of it, during that incident where it was falsely claimed that Filo-tan’s Finacée had been kidnapped—while Father was being pursued—the place where I fought him… had somehow turned into a dense jungle. I heard later that he was managing seeds from plants he’d modified. The plants back then were probably modified to some extent by Father so they wouldn’t wither.

However, the seeds Father is distributing to the people this time will produce plants of inferior quality. If they’re neglected, they’ll wither… By creating plants that are just a bit tougher than usual, he’s testing the people. To see if they’re managing them properly and seriously.

Those who let them wither are irresponsible and, when in trouble, commit foolish acts like invading other territories. If they manage them seriously, no problems will arise. It seems that my Father has thought this through to ensure a smooth cycle. However, simply giving them away isn’t enough.

Come to think of it, I remember that my Father was also conscious of soil management back in the village. He used to give all sorts of instructions to the monsters tasked with tending the fields. In the end, he got playfully tackled by one of the soil-tending monsters and ended up half-buried in the field; he had to be rescued by Big Sister and the village slaves.

“Things were going well for a while… but… I’d be in trouble if people started saying, ‘It’s all the Shield Hero’s fault that this village was destroyed!’ So I have to be careful about when I distribute them.”
My Father proceeds to modify the Bio-Plant seeds.

“I’ll have to make sure he takes responsibility for any Bio-Plants that wither. Even if I make them sturdy enough not to wither… if they aren’t properly tended, they might still die, and ultimately, the plants might be driven from their homes. It’d be a disaster if this place turned into a ‘Land of Death,’ wouldn’t it?”

That’s a bit of a hard pill to swallow. Given the bio-plants’ mutability, there’s no doubt the seeds I handed out put the village to the southwest in a difficult situation. If that happens, the trust placed in me as a saint could easily turn against me.
I suppose that’s what Father is worried about. That’s why I have to exercise the utmost caution when handing them out—and sell the seeds instead.
“All right, now that I’ve finished modifying the plants to produce sturdy fruits for peddling, I think I’ll ask Elena to lend me some of her land.”
“Booh…”
“Yeah, if things go well, I’ll be able to make some money, too.”
And so, my immediate sales plan proceeded steadily forward.
